quarters.name: Foundation & MVP Definition
quarters.objective: Convert StartupHub from concept into a clearly defined, usable MVP.
workstreams: Finalise core institutional problem and target users
Finalise MVP scope and user journeys
quarters.outcome: A functional MVP ready for controlled institutional testing.

quarters.name: Integrated MVP & Pilot Preparation
quarters.objective: Connect the major ecosystem workflows and prepare the product for real users.
quarters.outcome: An integrated product ready for pilot deployment.

quarters.name: Institutional Pilot & Product Refinement
quarters.objective: Put StartupHub into real institutional environments and measure actual usage.
workstreams: Measure time saved and process improvement
Prioritise features based on real usage
quarters.outcome: Validated product with measurable pilot results and evidence of institutional demand.

quarters.name: Launch Readiness & Early Commercialisation
quarters.objective: Convert the validated MVP into a market-ready product.
workstreams: Convert pilot institutions into paying customers
quarters.outcome: Market-ready StartupHub with pilot evidence, initial institutional customers and a clear scale-up pathway.

budget.name: Technology Development & Innovation Refinement
budget.note: Core product, then ecosystem integration, then pilot hardening, then production readiness.

budget.name: Market Research & Pilot Study
budget.note: Front-loaded cheaply, weighted to the pilot quarters, and heaviest in Q4 when willingness-to-pay has to be tested.

budget.name: IP Filing & Management
budget.note: Check DPIIT facilitator benefits and statutory fee schedules before committing this line.

budget.name: Incubation & Mentorship
budget.note: Flat across the year - the only line that does not flex.

budget.name: Startup Registration & Consultation
budget.note: Starts in Q2, once there is a product to register.

budget.name: Competitions / Exhibitions
budget.note: Late-year, and travel only where explicitly eligible.

budget.name: Essential Contingency
budget.note: A controlled reserve for essential unforeseen MVP/pilot requirements, subject to approval and funding rules. Not 'extra money'.

artefacts: Controlled reserve for essential unforeseen MVP/pilot requirements, subject to approval and funding rules

story_arc.phrase: the platform through real institutional pilots
the validated product into market readiness and early commercial adoption

investor_story: StartupHub will use the first quarter to establish the MVP foundation, the second quarter to integrate the core ecosystem, the third quarter to validate the platform through real institutional pilots, and the fourth quarter to transition the validated product into market readiness and early commercial adoption.
framing_statement: Rs 6 lakh is the estimated first-year MVP-to-market requirement, derived from the planned development, validation, IP, incubation, registration and pilot activities across four defined milestones. Individual cost heads will be supported through quotations, official fee schedules, vendor estimates, or institutional documentation wherever applicable.
milestone_question: What milestone does this money help us achieve?

unverified.title: No rupee in this budget is evidenced
unverified.claim: The full Rs 6,00,000 across 7 lines and 4 quarters.
unverified.checked: Arithmetic. Every row total, every column total and the grand total were recomputed and agree.
unverified.open: Not one line has a quotation behind it. This is a planning estimate, and it must not be submitted as a costed proposal until the evidence register in 04_Funding_Evidence.md is filled.

unverified.title: The cited MIC document is a 2020 contest guide
unverified.claim: That MIC's innovation framework 'expects a clear progression from idea/PoC toward prototype, with defined milestones, resources, mentoring and validation'.
unverified.checked: The cited PDF was retrieved and read (20 pages). It is the IIC National Innovation Contest 2020 portal submission guide. It does document the idea -> PoC -> prototype progression, TRL banding, evaluation by the IIC with a score of 25 of 50 for approval, and mentoring of approved prototypes.
unverified.open: It is a contest guide for 2020, not the current general IIC handholding framework, and it does not state the 'cost, beneficiaries, impact and scalability' framing. That framing comes from a different MIC document which has not been identified or retrieved. Do not attribute it to this PDF.

unverified.title: Startup India IP-fee benefits are unconfirmed
unverified.claim: That eligible DPIIT-recognised startups can access IP facilitators with the government bearing facilitator fees, and that patents receive an 80% filing-fee rebate.
unverified.checked: The Startup India scheme page was retrieved. It renders its substantive content through JavaScript and the text could not be read, so the claim was not confirmed.
unverified.open: Confirm against the current DPIIT benefits page or the relevant gazette notification before relying on either benefit. This matters: it is the reason the IP line is only Rs 30,000 and should not grow without checking first.

unverified.title: MIC eligibility for Rs 6 lakh is not established
unverified.claim: That Rs 6 lakh is the MIC-approved or eligible amount.
unverified.checked: Nothing. This document makes no such claim and the folder states so explicitly.
unverified.open: The specific current call and guidelines applicable to the institution must be checked. The MIC material establishes an innovation-development and handholding framework, which is not by itself enough to infer eligibility for every proposed expense head.

unverified.title: Incorporation cost is not quantified here
unverified.claim: That private-company incorporation carries statutory costs plus professional fees, varying by circumstance and state.
unverified.checked: Stated as a variable, not a number. The folder asserts no amount.
unverified.open: The MCA and government fee schedules and the professional quotation will settle the Startup Registration line.

unverified.title: Market demand behind the roadmap is not evidenced
unverified.claim: That institutions will buy, and at what price.
unverified.checked: Nothing in this folder supports it. The pilot in Q3 and the willingness-to-pay assessment in Q4 are the activities that would test it.
unverified.open: Q3's pricing validation and willingness-to-pay assessment are the first point at which this claim becomes testable. Until then it is an assumption, and the Q3 and Q4 budgets should be understood as buying the test.
